chapter: Medicine show, hoboing and train songs
title: Learning 'Big Rock Candy Mountain' on the medicine show; hoboing to Asheville
summary: After singing 'Big Rock Candy Mountain', Nash says he learned it on a medicine show, hearing it from a West Virginia guitarist. When a show got stranded he hoboed to Asheville, played ukulele at a theater and a club, then returned to New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: In the months of May, a sunny day, a boyly bum come hiking down the shady land to the sugar can. He was looking for his liking. And he rolled along and he sung a song with a blend of milk and honey. Where a bum can stay for many of days. And he don't need any money. Of the button of the bees and the cigarette trees. So the water fountain. The lemonade spring. Where's the bluebird sing? In the big rock candy mountain. And then on the run come a fireman's son. Through the hay field he was abounding. Says the bum to the sun. Why don't you come to the big rock candy mountain? Then the very night they hiked away. Well, the milestone thing was counting. The lemonade spring. Where's the bluebird sing? The big rock candy mountain. Where'd you learn that lemon? I learned that when I was on the medicine show. I was on the medicine show. I used to be with the big Indian man. And Western Cowboy. You know selling medicine. You know they'd sell all this pattern medicine. Through the country. Selling that Royalene Blood Tony.
Well who taught it to you?

Well I heard a fellow out of West Virginia. Was playing on a guitar one time. And I heard him sing that. So I caught it right there from him. Did you do any hoboing yourself ever? Well one time I quit a show and I had to hobo. The show got stranded. And I hoboed. I hoboed to Asheville. Asheville, North Carolina. And then when I got in Asheville. I got a job at the theater there. The Eagle Theater on Eagle Street. Singing and playing ukulele on the stage. And then things got bad there. So some police had a club there. And they used to come and get me and another guy a guitar to play out there at the club. And we played there. And I got over some money. Saved it. And about two months later I came on back to New Orleans.
